sections.text: Small steps add up. In a typical week, we meet about 120 different people. We have served 13,705 meals since 2024. Every
sections.words: Small steps add up. In a typical week, we meet about 120 different people. We have served 13,705 meals since 2024. Every day, our peers answer about 10 questions about where to find something, who to call, or what comes next. Each year, about 20 people we have worked with reach stable housing. 5 where we gave basic needs. We count the connection, but we do not claim the housing. 10 where we are part of a larger care team. 5 where we are the primary support. Of the people who reach housing with us as their primary support, 4 out of 5 found their own way there. Self-resolutions are individual paths home that the person chose and pursued. Numbers as of October 2026, from the Boulder Feet Forward information packet. See our impact

sections.words: Small steps add up. In a typical week, we meet about 120 different people. We have served 13,705 meals since 2024. Every day, our peers answer about 10 questions about where to find something, who to call, or what comes next. Each year, about 20 people we have worked with reach stable housing. 5 where we gave basic needs. We count the connection, but we do not claim the housing. 10 where we are part of a larger care team. 5 where we are the primary support. Of the people who reach housing with us as their primary support, 4 out of 5 found their own way there. Self-resolutions are individual paths home that the person chose and pursued. sections.words: Boulder Feet Forward exists to enable and support stability. We are peers. We are members of our community. We visit our neighbors every day. And we do what we can to meet our community’s needs. We offer meals to those who are hungry. We offer supplies to those who need them. We offer our presence to those who just want to talk. We find resources for those who ask. We offer our guidance as peers to those who want it. We offer our advocacy as case managers to those who are ready to progress. We believe in a person-first approach: no single solution fits every individual, and we’re here to help each person find the one that works best for them. Everything we do keeps in mind that each person is the main character in their own story. We’re here to support, not to prescribe. We’re here to help establish and build self-sufficiency. We’re here each day, letting our neighbors and peers know they can come to us for help when they’re ready. We’re here each day to provide what stabilization we can until then. We’re here each day so that our neighbors and peers get to know us, and come to understand that when they’re ready, our focus will be on their personal journey and their own definition of success. Every day. Step by step.

sections.words: Boulder Feet Forward exists to enable and support stability. We are peers. We are members of our community. We visit our neighbors every day. And we do what we can to meet our community’s needs. We offer meals to those who are hungry. We offer supplies to those who need them. We offer our presence to those who just want to talk. We find resources for those who ask. We offer our guidance as peers to those who want it. We offer our advocacy as case managers to those who are ready to progress. We believe in a person-first approach: no single solution fits every individual, and we’re here to help each person find the one that works best for them. Everything we do keeps in mind that each person is the main character in their own story. We’re here to support, not to prescribe. We’re here to help establish and build self-sufficiency. We’re here each day, letting our neighbors and peers know they can come to us for help when they’re ready. We’re here each day to provide what stabilization we can until then. We’re here each day so that our neighbors and peers get to know us, and come to understand that when they’re ready, our focus will be on their personal journey and their own definition of success. Every day. Step by step.

sections.text: What meeting people where they are looks like. Twice a week, zero-barrier outreach events Nutritious meals, hygiene supp
sections.words: What meeting people where they are looks like. Twice a week, zero-barrier outreach events Nutritious meals, hygiene supplies, clothing and weather gear, first aid, harm reduction supplies, pet care supplies and more. We provide the infrastructure, food and hygiene supplies. Partners, volunteers and donors expand what is on the table, and providers get a reliable place to meet people who may never walk through their doors. We solve the problem in front of us A bus pass, a bike lock, glasses, laundry, a shower, a haircut, a bike or car repair, a safe place to park, a phone call. If the resource exists, we help people reach it, and we spend our own dollars only where we find gaps. It is whatever small thing is standing between someone and their next step. We help people navigate services and systems Coordinated Entry from wherever you are. Housing assessments on site. IDs and documents, social benefits, health and behavioral health care, employment, education and volunteer opportunities, legal resources, treatment, sober living and many pathways to recovery. Trained peers help with applications, phone calls, paperwork, rides and the next step. We make warm handoffs, not just referrals We introduce people to providers, help them through intake, advocate when needed, get them to appointments, follow up afterward and coordinate with existing care teams. If something does not work, we troubleshoot, try something else and learn from it. We create connection, community and belonging Workshops and useful information, art and poetry, movies and games, trauma-informed movement and more. Belonging is part of stability.

sections.words: What meeting people where they are looks like. Twice a week, zero-barrier outreach events Nutritious meals, hygiene supplies, clothing and weather gear, first aid, harm reduction supplies, pet care supplies and more. We provide the infrastructure, food and hygiene supplies. Partners, volunteers and donors expand what is on the table, and providers get a reliable place to meet people who may never walk through their doors. We solve the problem in front of us A bus pass, a bike lock, glasses, laundry, a shower, a haircut, a bike or car repair, a safe place to park, a phone call. If the resource exists, we help people reach it, and we spend our own dollars only where we find gaps. It is whatever small thing is standing between someone and their next step. We help people navigate services and systems Coordinated Entry from wherever you are. Housing assessments on site. IDs and documents, social benefits, health and behavioral health care, employment, education and volunteer opportunities, legal resources, treatment, sober living and many pathways to recovery. Trained peers help with applications, phone calls, paperwork, rides and the next step. We make warm handoffs, not just referrals We introduce people to providers, help them through intake, advocate when needed, get them to appointments, follow up afterward and coordinate with existing care teams. If something does not work, we troubleshoot, try something else and learn from it. We create connection, community and belonging Workshops and useful information, art and poetry, movies and games, trauma-informed movement and more. Belonging is part of stability.

sections.words: What meeting people where they are looks like. Twice a week, zero-barrier outreach events Nutritious meals, hygiene supplies, clothing and weather gear, first aid, harm reduction supplies, pet care supplies and more. We provide the infrastructure, food and hygiene supplies. Partners, volunteers and donors expand what is on the table, and providers get a reliable place to meet people who may never walk through their doors. We solve the problem in front of us A bus pass, a bike lock, glasses, laundry, a shower, a haircut, a bike or car repair, a safe place to park, a phone call. If the resource exists, we help people reach it, and we spend our own dollars only where we find gaps. It is whatever small thing is standing between someone and their next step. We help people navigate services and systems Coordinated Entry from wherever you are. Housing assessments on site. IDs and documents, social benefits, health and behavioral health care, employment, education and volunteer opportunities, legal resources, treatment, sober living and many pathways to recovery. Trained peers help with applications, phone calls, paperwork, rides and the next step. We make warm handoffs, not just referrals We introduce people to providers, help them through intake, advocate when needed, get them to appointments, follow up afterward and coordinate with existing care teams. If something does not work, we troubleshoot, try something else and learn from it. We create connection, community and belonging Workshops and useful information, art and poetry, movies and games, trauma-informed movement and more. Belonging is part of stability.

sections.words: Skip to content Help us keep showing up. It is not just a handout. Your gift pays for the meals, and for the people who help someone find a way home. Give where it’s needed most Our work is much more than a handout. A direct gift keeps case management going: housing assessments, resource navigation, referrals, warm handoffs, benefits enrollment, peer support and advocacy. Give once, or give monthly. Monthly gifts are how we keep showing up. Give where it’s needed You will finish on our giving page at Zeffy. You can choose one time or monthly there. Fund something specific Choose what your gift does. Amounts are estimates from our recent costs. Community meals Purchased food fills the gaps in donated food, so we can serve about 458 nutritious meals every month. $19 buys food for about 10 meals. (approximate) Fund this Personal care supplies About 11,360 hygiene, first-aid and personal care items a year. People choose what they need, rather than getting pre-made kits. $27 stocks about 100 care items. (approximate) Fund this Laundry program Twenty vouchers a month at Wash and Wave in North Boulder, so people can reuse clothing, blankets and sleeping bags. $5 pays for one wash-and-dry load. (approximate) Fund this Transportation and mobility Half-price RTD passes through the nonprofit program: at least 370 rides a month to appointments, food banks, shelter and services. $14 buys a ten-ride pass. (approximate) Fund this Give things Your gently used items go to neighbors according to need. Our outreach events use single-use food service items, and we aim to use mostly compostable supplies. We also hand out seasonal survival gear. Our Amazon wish list lists what we use and distribute, and anything ordered ships directly to us. Open the wish list Donating items yourself The things our neighbors can use most: Bikes, bike locks and bicycle repair supplies Sturdy backpacks and other luggage Mobility aids such as canes, walkers and crutches Camping gear Water bottles Email us to arrange a drop-off. For clothing and shoes, please contact Deacon’s Closet. For furniture, contact Home Ahead. We are glad to send you to partners who can use those. Curious where it all goes? See how a year of giving is spent.

sections.words: The numbers In a typical week, we meet about 120 different people. Across both weekly events. About 85 come to Tuesdays in the Park. We have served 13,705 meals since 2024. Every day, our peers answer about 10 questions about where to find something, who to call, or what comes next. About two or three times a week, someone connects with a stabilizing resource, with our help. Each year, about 20 people we have worked with reach stable housing. 5 where we gave basic needs. We count the connection, but we do not claim the housing. 10 where we are part of a larger care team. 5 where we are the primary support. Of the people who reach housing with us as their primary support, 4 out of 5 found their own way there. Self-resolutions are individual paths home that the person chose and pursued. Volunteers gave about 424 hours at Tuesday events in 2024, worth at least $16,959. Tuesday outreach only. Friday hours are not included. Every day, our peers answer about 10 questions about where to find something, who to call, or what comes next. About two or three times a week, someone connects with a stabilizing resource, with our help. Each year, about 20 people we have worked with reach stable housing. 5 where we gave basic needs. We count the connection, but we do not claim the housing. 10 where we are part of a larger care team. 5 where we are the primary support. Of the people who reach housing with us as their primary support, 4 out of 5 found their own way there. Self-resolutions are individual paths home that the person chose and pursued. Volunteers gave about 424 hours at Tuesday events in 2024, worth at least $16,959. Tuesday outreach only. Friday hours are not included.
